pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome – Warden Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to our school website. I am very proud to share with you a glimpse into just some of the exciting opportunities and wonderful developments that shape daily life here at Warden Hill.
Our vision of Unlocking the Potential in Every Child sits at the heart of everything we do. It is more than a statement – it is a commitment. A commitment to ensuring that every child who walks through our doors feels known, valued and inspired to become the very best version of themselves.
Our values of Belong, Explore, Succeed underpin our curriculum, our culture and the way we work together. They are lived out in every classroom, every shared space and every moment of school life. They are also celebrated through our four houses – Leach, Windrush, Churn and Coln – which bring energy, pride and a deep sense of community to our school. These houses are the lifeblood of Warden Hill, connecting children across year groups and giving them opportunities to challenge themselves, support one another and shine.
The vast majority of parents want the same thing for their child in life: for them to be happy. It’s a simple word, yet it unlocks so much – confidence, curiosity, resilience and success. At Warden Hill, our children are extremely happy. They learn brilliantly from superb teaching, and they find success at every level – nothing is capped, and no child is ever defined by a limit.
Alongside our subject curriculums, we teach the life skills that help children understand themselves and the world around them: empathy, kindness, perseverance, resilience, what it means to be different, what it means to be the same, and how to navigate both success and challenge. These lessons happen in classrooms, in inter-house events, and in the countless small moments that make up a school day.
We are very much a team at Warden Hill. That team includes our staff, our governors, our wider community – and crucially, our families, who are our children’s first and most important educators. We believe deeply in working together, in partnership, to ensure every child receives the very best, because they deserve nothing less.
Please take time to explore our website, and I look forward to welcoming you to our school in person soon.

About
Our vision is to prepare our children not only for the next steps in their learning each year or for the next step to secondary, but to educate them and equip them for the world they are growing into. Shalom bambinos
By prioritising the skills of evaluation, perseverance and critical thinking and the characteristics of humility, empathy and relational connections, we will ensure that this journey is firmly established by the time they leave us.

Music
At Warden Hill all children experience a wealth of musical opportunities to create, participate and perform both individually and as part of a whole class ensemble. They will learn and appreciate music from around the world and develop a lifelong love for the subject. Children will have an opportunity to learn a musical instrument as well as have multiple opportunities to sing and play classroom instruments. Through actively participating in interactive sessions they will grow in confidence and develop their individual musicality.

Art
Warden Hill believes that art has a huge impact in all areas of the curriculum and children’s learning. We also recognise the enrichment and development opportunities that can be achieved through art and design.
With this in mind at Warden Hill we aim to equip each child with the knowledge and skills to explore their own creativity and create their own works of art whilst developing their critical thinking and assessment skills. Through a considered sequence of lessons and experiences our children will develop a wide range of art and design techniques in using colour, pattern, texture, line, shape, form and space.
These theories are delivered through the mediums of painting, drawing, printing, textiles and sculpture. The skills and knowledge that our children will develop throughout each art unit are mapped across each year group and throughout the school to ensure consistent progression.

Computing
At Warden Hill, we believe every child has the potential to thrive in our digital world. Our computing curriculum helps children feel they belong in a connected society, explore technology with confidence and curiosity and succeed by developing essential skills for the future.
Children learn to stay safe online, think creatively and solve problems through coding, data handling and digital media. They use laptops, iPads, VR headsets and we are now beginning to explore AI tools to enhance their learning. As children engage with artificial intelligence, we also teach them to understand both the exciting opportunities it offers and the challenges it presents.
Technology is a powerful tool across the curriculum, helping children express ideas, deepen understanding and unlock their potential. Our “Switched on Computing” scheme and our own Warden Hill Digital Literacy Skills Ladder ensure children develop practical skills using Word, Excel and PowerPoint alongside essential digital skills like saving, printing, and organising work.
Online safety is a key focus and (supported by our Golden Rules) is revisited regularly to help children make smart, informed choices in an ever-changing digital landscape.
By combining hands-on experiences with thoughtful guidance, we prepare our pupils not just to use technology — but to shape the future with it.

English
The English Subject Leader Group’s primary aim is to develop a passion for reading by exploring widespread and challenging texts as well as promoting reading for pleasure.
We will share diverse texts to all years to provide children to feel a sense of belonging and develop a wider understanding of the world around them. Reading widely, will allow them to be successful and confident writers able to express themselves articulately and develop a unique style. We strive for all children to have the ability to unpick key vocabulary as it will unlock many doors to allow our children opportunities to access and engage a deeper understanding within all areas of the curriculum.

French
The primary aim with French teaching is to develop a love of languages.
We ensure we offer a relevant, broad and ambitious curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils using a wide range of topics and themes.
All pupils will be given the opportunity to explore a new language through its vocabulary, grammar and phonetics. They will understand where they belong in the world through the study on another culture and how it links to our own, developing a better understanding of self. Pupils will succeed and achieve their full potential through the encouragement of high expectations.
The ultimate aim being that pupils will feel positive and confident about learning languages and be able to continue studying languages beyond key stage 2.

Geography
We aim to instil curiosity and fascination within our children to enable them to explore their world as geographers.
Our curriculum is meaningful to the children as it uses units of learning that directly relate to them and the community that they belong to. We strive to encourage the children we teach to ask questions about our impact upon the world and how we can make a positive difference.
Our children’s growing knowledge about the world will help them to have a greater understanding of diverse places and people.

History
Our primary aim is to foster a love of enquiry-based learning.
We want to create historians that are able to develop their skills and conceptual understanding through exploring and investigating the past. We strive to ensure our children have excellent opportunities to understand the chronology behind every time period they learn about.
In every lesson, our children are able to build on their previous learning with new knowledge, making connections between and across periods of time they have studied. We also recognise the value of teaching subject specific vocabulary to enhance our children’s understanding. Our teachers have high expectations and believe that every child has the ability to achieve and be a thoughtful and reflective historian.
We aim to deliver a History curriculum that is accessible to all and aspire to have our children leave Warden Hill with a breadth, depth and wealth of historical knowledge that will allow them to succeed.

Mathematics
Unlocking the potential in every child is at the heart of everything we do at Warden Hill. Guided by our core values — belong, explore, and succeed — we aim to inspire a lifelong love of mathematics in every child by nurturing curiosity, creativity, and confidence in their mathematical abilities.
We believe that mathematics is a gateway to understanding the world around us, and our teaching emphasises:
Each sequence of learning is carefully chosen to ensure coherence, enabling children to build on their prior knowledge and see clear connections between concepts. Every lesson is thoughtfully planned to develop fluency, encourage problem-solving, and incorporate variation to deepen understanding. Lessons are enriched with different representations and a focus on structure, ensuring concepts are presented in multiple ways to support all learners. Additionally, oracy is woven into every lesson, empowering children to articulate their mathematical thinking with clarity and confidence.
The impact of our approach is seen in the confident, curious mathematicians we nurture. Our children develop the ability to connect ideas, reason their answers, and notice patterns, fostering a deep and meaningful understanding of mathematics. They are engaged and enthusiastic learners who approach challenges with confidence, perseverance, and creativity. By equipping them with these skills, we aim to cultivate a genuine enjoyment of mathematics and empower them to become capable, reflective problem solvers both in school and in their future lives.

PSHE
At Warden Hill Primary School, our PSHE curriculum, strives to ensure that every pupil feels part of a caring community, is encouraged to discover their unique strengths, and is supported to achieve their very best, which supports our vision of ‘Unlocking the potential in every child.’Our PSHE curriculum is rooted in our school values:BelongWe aim to create a safe, inclusive environment where every child feels valued and respected. We strive for our children to develop a strong sense of identity and belonging within their school, community, and wider society and through positive relationships to learn empathy, kindness, and the importance of celebrating diversity.ExploreWe encourage our pupils to ask questions, challenge ideas, and explore the world around them with curiosity and confidence. In our lessons, the children will gain knowledge and skills to understand themselves, others, and the wider world, including health, wellbeing, and citizenship. Through this exploration we hope it will foster resilience, adaptability, and the ability to make informed choices in a changing society.SucceedOur curriculum empowers our children to set goals, persevere, and achieve their personal best. We endeavour to build confidence and independence in them so that they will be prepared to thrive in future learning and life experiences.Our aim is that the curriculum equips children with the knowledge, skills, and values they need to lead healthy, safe, and fulfilling lives, while preparing them to be responsible, resilient, and respectful members of society.

RSHE

We believe that high-quality Relationship, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) enables children to grow into confident, respectful, and responsible individuals who are well-prepared for the opportunities and challenges of modern Britain, which supports our vision of ‘Unlocking the potential in every child.’Our RSHE curriculum is rooted in our school values:Belong We ensure every child feels safe, included, and valued within our school community.ExploreWe encourage curiosity, open discussion, and age-appropriate learning about healthy relationships (on and off line), health, and personal development.SucceedWe equip children with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to make informed choices and flourish in their future lives.Our aim is that our curriculum supports our children to feel positive about themselves and their identity, have confidence when making choices about relationships and behaviours, building foundations for healthy and safe lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Design and Technology – Warden Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Design and Technology
Our children belong to an ever-developing world and our design and technology curriculum aims to equip them with the necessary skills needed for their future.
We are developing our lessons so that they provide opportunities for children to succeed by becoming independent, imaginative problem-solvers and thinkers, both as individuals and as part of a team. At Warden Hill, our children develop their skills through construction, textiles and cooking units.
Our primary aim is to ensure progression so that skills are discretely taught, revisited and refined throughout their time at our school.
This year, our newly created units of work aim to provide opportunities for children to explore, test and evaluate existing products. Our intention is for the children to then use their knowledge and skills to design and create their own quality product for a specified purpose.

pageCache.pageTitle: Physical Education – Warden Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Physical Education
At Warden Hill, our PE curriculum is designed to unlock the potential in every child. We strive to nurture resilient individuals who understand the value of physical activity in leading a balanced and fulfilling life.
BelongSport and physical activity bring our school community together in the most exciting and engaging way. We foster a safe, inclusive environment where every child feels valued and part of a team. Through collaborative activities, sportsmanship, and shared goals, children build strong relationships. Within our house system, all children develop a sense of belonging as they strive for success in a diverse array of sports during our house competitions.
ExploreOur curriculum develops children’s physical movement skills through a wide range of sports and activities so that they build strong foundations in the fundamental movement skills. Children are empowered to try new sports, challenge themselves, and develop a deeper understanding of health, fitness, and movement.
SucceedAt Warden Hill our curriculum ensures that, regardless of ability or background, all children have access to high-quality PE experiences. The carefully sequenced lessons and PE units in our scheme, build the children’s PE knowledge and understanding. We support every child to set personal goals, build resilience, and celebrate progress. Whether through a range of competitive sport events, personal bests, or teamwork, children experience the joy of achievement and the confidence to thrive.
Our aim for every child at Warden Hill to leave equipped with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to lead healthy, active lives and have developed love of physical movement which will be life-long.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development Curriculum – Warden Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Personal Development Curriculum
The vast majority of parents want the same thing for their child in life– for them to be happy. It’s quite a simple word, but actually, it is a word which is the key to unlock a host of other words when we talk about educating children: confidence, inquisitiveness and success, to name a few.
At Warden Hill our children are extremely happy. They learn brilliantly from superb teaching and they find success at whatever level – nothing is capped. Interwoven with teaching our bespoke subject curriculums, is also the teaching of life skills: values, morals, empathy, how to stay safe, kindness, what it is to be different, what it is to be the same, what success is, what failure is, what perseverance is, what resilience is, what friendship is, what it is to be them.
This, in essence, is what we call our Personal Development curriculum. The curriculum is made up of the following areas:
We develop healthy, happy, friendly and independent children.
Our excellent range of extracurricular clubs for all age groups.
We support our children’s developing knowledge, understanding, attitudes and practical skills to live healthy, safe, productive and fulfilled lives both now and in the future.
We develop respectful, resilient, confident and kind children through our values, the Warden Hill Way and our characteristics of effective learning.
We aim for everyone to identify with our community, and have a sense of belonging, where equity of opportunities allows all children to thrive and find success. [Equality and diversity page]
We promote democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. It is essential that we ensure all of these are promoted and respected, to enable our children to grow and develop their own personal values, showing tolerance of others’.
[British Values page]
‘The British Values are like puzzle pieces – each one a vital component in one’s life: they are all implemented in a pupils’ time here at Warden Hill in so many ways.’
‘Being a student of Warden Hill School the British Values have been a big part of my life. They have been weaved into lessons and make us who we are.’
We create global citizens, who think about their actions understand communities, social justice, and the environment.
Lyfta invites students to experience different cultures and perspectives. It gives them the opportunity to see and connect with positive human stories from around the world – modelling resilience, problem-solving, teamwork, and many other critical skills, values and competencies.Lyfta helps teachers nurture the global citizens of tomorrow.
https://www.lyfta.com/
We show the awe and wonder in the world, communities and within ourselves.
We provide a wide range of opportunities from arts to sport for all, which add to the children’s cultural capital and enriches their lives.
[Patron of Reading page]
Personal development is such a strength of our school and is exceptional. We provide support for pupils’ personal development through our in-class and wider curriculum and our Year 6 pupils leave us knowledgeable, well-rounded, resilient and confident children.Our curriculum ensures our children have varied experiences, which equip them with an excellent understanding of the Fundamental British Values with which to grow up in modern Britain. Our ultimate goal is to develop our children to be aware of and to respect, the beliefs and opinions of others and to be tolerant and respectful of our school and wider community. We also aim to give them skills to succeed in life by supporting their well-being and mental health.
We set great store in exploring and taking learning further afield. Our Forest school programme of outdoor learning is excellent and widely recognised as so, but we also organise many trips outside of school. They are our way of enriching our pupils’ learning opportunities, giving even more depth and value to the experiences they receive in their classrooms. Such visits help to maintain the motivation to learn and support the children in retaining even more knowledge. Past trips have included Bristol Zoo, We The Curious, Bisley, Bishops Wood, The Forest of Dean, Cheltenham High Street, Crickley Hill, Pittville Park and Pump Rooms, Avebury Stones, Clevedon Pier and a journey on the Winchcombe steam train as evacuees!
We are in a very privileged position to be part of this learning process – a process which is firmly embedded in our school values – Belong – Explore – Succeed. They underpin all we do at our School and it creates a very special place. Through their time with us, all our pupils will have had access to a wide range of diverse experiences which will ensure they are fully prepared for their next educational journey to secondary school.
When they leave us, they do so with a smile, with confidence, with resilience and an understanding and acquisition of the skills and personal qualities that will support them now and into adult life.

Please note that submitting the form does not guarantee your child’s place at the club.If we receive more entries than places available, the names will be chosen at random. You will receive a confirmation if your child has been selected. Children who are not successful, will be put on the waiting list.
